issues.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat in a historic upset
issues.gist: Democrat Scott Colom won a US Senate seat in Mississippi in a very close race. He will be the state's first Black senator in more than 150 years.
issues.gistKo: 민주당의 스콧 콜롬이 아주 근소한 차로 미시시피주 연방 상원 의석을 차지했어요. 그는 150년 넘게 만에 이 주의 첫 흑인 상원의원이 돼요.
issues.easyKo: 미시시피주 상원 선거에서 민주당 후보 스콧 콜롬이 아주 적은 표 차이로 이겼어요. 이 주가 직접 선거로 뽑은 첫 흑인 상원의원이라서 역사적인 일로 불려요. 앞으로 그가 공약을 지킬 수 있을지가 관심이에요.

views.view: BBC says young voters and Black voters helped Colom win, and calls the result historic for the state.
ABC says the win breaks the idea that Mississippi results are fixed, but one win does not prove lasting change.

why: A Democrat won a Senate seat in a state that had not elected one since 1982.
He will be the first Black senator the state's voters have elected directly.
lines.agree: Observers agree the result is a historic first for Mississippi.
lines.split: It is unclear whether this win marks lasting change or one special election.
lines.life: US Senate votes shape laws on jobs, health care and prices, which can reach students and workers far outside America.
lines.next: Watch the Alaska race and whether Colom can keep his promises on wages, rural hospitals and living costs.

talk.answer: In Mississippi, the race was decided by about 4,700 votes, and the BBC said young people helped Colom. When a race is this close, every group that turns out can change the result. I think this shows that voting is worth the effort.

paragraphs.en: Democrat Scott Colom has won a US Senate seat in Mississippi, beating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. The race was so close that it took more than a week to call. The Associated Press said that, with 99% of the expected vote counted, Colom had 49.2% and Hyde-Smith had 48.7%. His lead was about 4,700 votes. Hyde-Smith called him to concede and said she respected the decision of Mississippi voters.

pro.en: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly unseated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, in a contest so tight that it took more than a week for the result to be called. With 99% of the expected vote reported, The Associated Press said Colom held 49.2% to her 48.7%, a margin of roughly 4,700 votes. Hyde-Smith telephoned him to concede and said she respected the decision of Mississippi voters.

Colom will become Mississippi's first Black senator in more than 150 years and only the third in the nation's history. His predecessors, Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce, served in the 1870s after the Civil War and were selected by the state legislature, which makes Colom the first Black senator elected directly by the state's voters. Mississippi had not seated a Democrat in the chamber since 1982.

A district attorney for four counties along the Mississippi-Alabama line, Colom was initially regarded as a long shot but built considerable buzz in the closing months of the campaign, appearing alongside former President Bill Clinton and former Vice President Kamala Harris. The BBC reported that young people and Mississippi's large Black electorate propelled his bid, with first-time voters at Jackson State University among his backers.

An ABC News analysis argued that the result undermines the assumption that Mississippi's statewide outcomes are foregone conclusions, while cautioning that a single victory does not establish a durable realignment. In its view, the decisive question is whether the coalition behind Colom can outlast him and this political moment. He campaigned on raising wages, protecting rural hospitals and easing the cost of living.

Colom's win is the eighth Senate seat Democrats have captured from Republicans, with the contest in Alaska still unresolved. Once sworn in, he will wield the same authority as every other senator, including votes on legislation and judicial nominations. Attention will now turn to whether he can fulfil the promises he made to Mississippians.

pro.en: An Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, killed six people and wounded 28 others on Thursday morning, according to The Guardian, with health authorities saying a surgeon was among the dead. It was the first attack on a medical facility since the truce took hold last October.

The Israeli military said it had targeted a Hamas commander and other militants at the site, but The Guardian noted that no evidence accompanied the claim. The newspaper added that roughly four Palestinians have been dying daily, on average, since the ceasefire was announced.

Meanwhile, torrential rain has compounded the hardship of displaced residents. UNICEF said at least six people, among them children, died in the storms, while local authorities reported that at least 70,000 tents flooded and more than 200,000 people were affected. Al Jazeera put the number living in flood-prone areas at about 950,000, and aid teams have started clearing blocked sewer lines at 60 locations, the United Nations reported. Al Jazeera also described how rainwater can wreck the solar systems families rely on for lighting and phone charging.

Israeli officials say 91,000 tents and more than 8,200 trucks carrying blankets and other supplies have entered Gaza in recent months, yet the Board of Peace, the body President Trump created to oversee the truce, has called those steps insufficient. Israel maintains that reconstruction cannot begin until Hamas fully disarms, a stance that Professor Nathan Brown told DW lies behind the slow progress, and an international assessment estimates that recovery will cost about $71.4 billion over the next decade.

Gadi Eisenkot has six weeks to assemble a government following last month’s election, and The Guardian argues that outside governments should apply sustained pressure for greater aid while the winter cold is already proving lethal. For Korean students, the episode illustrates how a ceasefire on paper can coexist with continuing danger for civilians.

views.view: The editorial says the strike was not an exception and that outside countries must press hard for more aid this winter.
It describes how rain floods tents, damages solar power and leaves families without light, with 950,000 people living in flood-prone areas.
It reports both Israel’s aid figures and the Board of Peace’s warning, and a professor says the stalled peace plan is tied to the disarmament dispute.

issues.title: Trump Says US Does Not Need an Iran Deal and Moves Vance Off the Talks
issues.gist: President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran and told Vice President Vance to focus on other work. Hours later, Iran said it hit a US radar in Bahrain, and ships in the Strait of Hormuz were still at risk.

pro.en: President Donald Trump declared on Thursday that Washington has no need for a deal with Tehran. The statement accompanied a social media post redirecting Vice President JD Vance, the administration's chief negotiator, toward what Trump described as corruption and crime in Democratic-run cities and states.

Vance had led talks in Islamabad in April that helped yield a memorandum of understanding in June, but the accord quickly unravelled because each side read its terms differently. The dispute centered on control of the Strait of Hormuz. After Republicans suffered sweeping midterm losses, Vance publicly blamed the war, while Trump acknowledged that rising fuel prices contributed to the defeat yet defended his decision to strike Iran.

In his post, Trump asserted that the United States already holds hundreds of billions of dollars of Iranian money and controls the strait. A White House official told ABC News that the naval blockade and economic pressure would continue, without confirming whether negotiations had ended. Al Jazeera noted visible divisions within the administration, since Secretary of State Marco Rubio has argued that economic pressure is working. Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, insisted the waterway would never return to its prewar status.

Within hours, Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed it had destroyed a US early warning radar in Bahrain, in retaliation for an American strike on a telecommunications pole in the port of Sirik. CBS News described it as Iran's first such claim involving Bahrain since September. The Guard also reported that a gas carrier struck a naval mine near the strait, even as the US military maintains that it has cleared shipping routes of mines. In peacetime, roughly one-fifth of global oil moved through that waterway.

Considerable uncertainty remains over whether Washington will continue contacts with Tehran through Qatari and Pakistani mediators. Observers will be watching whether the exchange of strikes escalates or stays contained, and whether commercial vessels can transit the strait without being hit.

issues.title: Harry Kane Sets England Caps Record and Scores the Winner Against Croatia
issues.gist: Harry Kane played his 126th match for England, more than any other man, and scored the winning penalty in a 2-1 win over Croatia. England are already in the Nations League quarter-finals.
issues.gistKo: 해리 케인이 잉글랜드 남자 대표팀 역대 최다인 126번째 경기에 나서 결승 페널티킥을 넣어 크로아티아를 2-1로 이겼어요. 잉글랜드는 이미 네이션스리그 8강에 올랐어요.
issues.easyKo: 잉글랜드 주장 케인이 대표팀 최다 출전 기록을 세운 날 직접 결승골까지 넣었어요. 경기 내용은 아쉬웠지만 기록의 밤은 승리로 마무리됐고, 이제 일요일 스페인전이 남았어요.

paragraphs.en: On Thursday night at Wembley, Harry Kane played his 126th match for England. That passed the old record of Peter Shilton and made Kane the most capped men's player in England history. England beat Croatia 2-1 in a Nations League game. The 33-year-old captain also scored the winning goal, his 92nd for England.

Shilton, Luka Modric and Prince William each gave him a gift. Modric, a former Tottenham teammate, gave a replica of the first football brought to Croatia, and William gave a framed shirt.

paragraphs.en: The Guardian said the football felt like a sideshow, and ESPN said England's defence remains a concern. pro.en: Harry Kane became England's most-capped men's player on Thursday at Wembley, winning his 126th cap and edging one ahead of Peter Shilton's long-standing record. The captain, aged 33, then supplied the decisive goal, his 92nd for his country, as England prevailed 2-1 over Croatia in a Nations League fixture played in London.

The pre-match programme was lavish, with Kane leading out his four children and displaying his Ballon d'Or to the stands beneath a giant tifo hailing him as "England's finest". Shilton, Luka Modric and Prince William each made a presentation to the England captain in a quick succession of gifts before the game began. Modric, a former Tottenham teammate, handed over a replica of the first football brought to Croatia, while the prince gave Kane a framed commemorative shirt.

Morgan Rogers gave England the lead after 24 minutes, finishing a move that Kane started with a diagonal ball to Jude Bellingham, but Petar Sucic levelled in the 59th minute. The equaliser followed a poorly judged back-header from Jarell Quansah toward the goalkeeper. Video review then ruled that Ivan Smolcic had tugged Quansah's shirt, and Kane converted the penalty in the 64th minute to settle the contest.

Reviewers were guarded about the performance, with the Guardian calling the football a sideshow to the celebrations and ESPN flagging England's defence as a continuing concern. ESPN noted that the back four had never started a match together and that two centre-backs were injured, while coach Thomas Tuchel praised Kane's hard work, talent and focus. Kane credited the 41-year-old Modric with inspiring him to push the limits, and he said he wanted to win a major trophy at Euro 2028.

England are guaranteed a place in the quarter-finals in March, having already secured their berth with the win at Wembley. On Sunday they travel to Madrid to face Spain, a fixture that will settle which side tops the group, and ESPN regards 100 international goals as Kane's next milestone.

views.view: The night was about celebrating Kane, and the football itself felt flat until his penalty changed the game.
England won, but the defence looked shaky and weak at set pieces, which is a worry before the Spain game.
Kane says he is inspired by Modric and wants to keep playing at the top level for as long as he can.

paragraphs.en: The move follows two days of talks between the United States, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. Those talks brought no breakthrough, but the sides agreed on a new swap of prisoners. pro.en: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on Thursday, then travelled to Dublin to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Both camps said European representatives would be seated at the next round of negotiations on ending the war, a development Zelensky welcomed after years of lobbying.

The announcement followed two days of trilateral talks among Washington, Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi that produced no breakthrough, although the sides agreed to another prisoner exchange. Kushner described it as the largest such swap since the full-scale invasion began in 2022, but offered no figures on how many detainees would be freed or when. Putin, for his part, said Moscow's position on the war, including its territorial demands, remains unchanged despite a day of intensive shuttle diplomacy.

At the European Political Community summit in Dublin, leaders failed to settle on a single figure to speak for the continent in any future negotiations. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Council President Antonio Costa are regarded as the likeliest candidates, yet many national leaders want to attend in person. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni rebuked the bloc in a letter to Costa, arguing that projecting disarray merely serves those who wish to prolong the war. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz insisted that Ukraine, the Europeans, the Americans and Russia must all be seated at the negotiating table.

Behind the procedural wrangling lies a deeper anxiety that a European seat at the table could come at a price, notably changes to the continent's security arrangements. Putin has indicated that his demands could include a guarantee that Ukraine never joins NATO, and he branded any European troops deployed after a settlement a legitimate target. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal questioned why Europe should debate its own defence with the very party that poses the threat. Analysts writing in The Conversation noted that ceasefire terms, the status of occupied territory and long-term security guarantees for Ukraine all remain unsettled.

Fighting continued meanwhile, with The Guardian reporting that Russia struck a hospital in central Kyiv. Zelensky said fresh restrictions on the Starshield satellite service had hampered Ukraine's ability to intercept incoming drones. The immediate question for Brussels and national capitals is who will represent Europe when the next round of negotiations begins.

issues.title: Pegula Saves a Match Point to Reach WTA Finals Semifinals as Gauff Goes Out
issues.gist: American Jessica Pegula saved a match point and beat Linda Noskova in three sets at the WTA Finals. The win sent her to the semifinals and knocked out her fellow American Coco Gauff.

sents.ko: BBC는 여자테니스협회(WTA) 의장도 페굴라에게 사과했다고 전했어요.

paragraphs.en: The tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells because of the United States-Israel war on Iran. Andreeva reached the semifinals by beating Aryna Sabalenka, according to BBC. Fans in Korea can follow the matches online and see how the long season has hurt many players. Watch the Pegula and Andreeva semifinal on Saturday.

sents.en: Watch the Pegula and Andreeva semifinal on Saturday.
sents.ko: 토요일 페굴라와 안드레예바의 준결승을 지켜보세요.

pro.en: American Jessica Pegula saved a match point en route to a 7-6, 4-6, 7-5 victory over Linda Noskova on Thursday, booking a WTA Finals semifinal berth in Indian Wells, California, and eliminating compatriot Coco Gauff from the season-ending championships.

All three players finished the round-robin phase 2-1, leaving set records to separate them: Noskova topped the group at 5-2, Pegula followed at 5-3 and Gauff stood at 4-3, while Pegula struck a career-high 16 aces against a career-high 15 double faults from Noskova over a see-saw contest of two hours and 45 minutes.

Gauff had earlier defeated alternate Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5, rallying from 1-5 down in the second set to win six straight games despite receiving treatment on her back, and Kostyuk, who replaced the ill Elena Rybakina, went winless in three matches while battling a wrist problem.

Pegula now meets Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva for the first time in Saturday's semifinal, an encounter spiced by her earlier remarks, caught on a livestream of a practice session, that Andreeva was "a diva" who "needs to be humbled", comments for which she apologized and which also praised the opponent as fast, strong and smart.

The tournament was relocated from Riyadh to Indian Wells because of the United States-Israel war on Iran, and BBC reported that Andreeva had already advanced by beating Aryna Sabalenka, setting up a Saturday semifinal that observers in Korea and elsewhere can follow online.

issues.title: Microsoft's Global Outage Knocks Out Email and Work Tools Worldwide
issues.gist: A big Microsoft outage stopped Outlook and other work tools in many countries. Microsoft says it was not a cyberattack and is working to bring services back.
issues.gistKo: 마이크로소프트의 큰 장애로 여러 나라에서 아웃룩 같은 업무 도구가 멈췄어요. 마이크로소프트는 사이버 공격이 아니라고 하며 서비스를 되살리는 중이에요.
issues.easyKo: 목요일부터 마이크로소프트의 이메일, 팀즈, AI 비서가 세계 곳곳에서 먹통이 됐어요. 회사는 서버가 갑자기 많이 빠지며 남은 서버에 부담이 몰렸고 해킹은 아니라고 말해요. 병원, 경찰, 학교, 정부 기관까지 영향을 받았어요.

paragraphs.en: A huge Microsoft outage began on Thursday, Nov. 12, and shut down email and other work tools around the world. Outlook was hit hardest, while Teams and the AI assistant Copilot also had problems. The tracking site Downdetector received reports from 74 countries within about an hour. More than 130,000 users reported trouble with Outlook, but the real number is probably much higher. Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its 365 apps.
paragraphs.ko: 11월 12일 목요일에 마이크로소프트에서 큰 장애가 시작되어 전 세계의 이메일과 업무 도구가 멈췄어요. 아웃룩이 가장 큰 타격을 받았고, 팀즈와 AI 비서 코파일럿도 문제를 겪었어요. 장애 추적 사이트 다운디텍터에는 약 한 시간 안에 74개 나라에서 신고가 들어왔어요. 13만 명이 넘는 사용자가 아웃룩 문제를 신고했지만, 실제 숫자는 훨씬 더 많을 것으로 보여요. 마이크로소프트는 자사 365 앱을 쓰는 사람이 4억 3천만 명이 넘는다고 해요.

paragraphs.en: Microsoft said the problem was not a cyberattack. Instead, it said part of its system had an "elevated load" after a large number of servers suddenly became unavailable. That pushed extra traffic onto the remaining servers and put them under strain. Some restarted servers failed again when traffic came back, and the first fixes did not work as expected. By Friday morning, the company reported early signs of stabilisation and progress in the Asia Pacific region, but warned that some problems could continue.
paragraphs.ko: 마이크로소프트는 이번 문제가 사이버 공격 때문이 아니라고 밝혔어요. 대신 많은 서버가 갑자기 쓸 수 없게 되면서 시스템 일부에 "높은 부하"가 걸렸다고 설명했어요. 그 때문에 남은 서버로 접속이 더 몰리면서 부담이 커졌어요. 다시 켠 서버 가운데 일부는 접속이 돌아오자 또 멈췄고, 첫 번째 수리 시도도 기대한 대로 되지 않았어요. 금요일 아침에 회사는 안정을 찾는 초기 신호와 아시아태평양 지역의 진전을 알렸지만, 일부 문제는 이어질 수 있다고 경고했어요.

paragraphs.en: The effects spread far beyond office email. In Britain, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police forces and schools were affected. Government systems in Singapore and Japan were disrupted, and so were the Supreme Court of the Philippines and Australia's spy agency and federal police. In Germany, the rail operator Deutsche Bahn said it was hard to send out timetables for diverted trains. OpenAI and Anthropic also said that tools connecting their AI services to Microsoft 365 were not working as expected.
paragraphs.ko: 영향은 사무실 이메일을 훨씬 넘어 퍼졌어요. 영국에서는 동네 병원, 약국, 경찰, 학교가 영향을 받았어요. 싱가포르와 일본의 정부 시스템이 차질을 빚었고, 필리핀 대법원과 호주의 정보기관, 연방경찰도 영향을 받았어요. 독일에서는 철도 운영사 도이체반이 우회 열차의 시간표를 내보내기 어려웠다고 밝혔어요. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽도 자사 AI 서비스를 마이크로소프트 365에 잇는 도구가 기대대로 작동하지 않는다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Microsoft had not yet published a root cause, so experts and officials gave their own views. Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft believed it faced something like the 2024 CrowdStrike outage, where an update went awry. Technology analyst Rupert Goodwins told Al Jazeera that the scale was impressive but not unprecedented. He said a faulty internal update is one common cause of such overload. Security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC that the outage shows how important email still is for work, appointments and online accounts. A tech expert writing in The Conversation said people and organisations should prepare for digital outages much as they prepare for natural disasters.
paragraphs.ko: 마이크로소프트가 아직 근본 원인을 공개하지 않아서 전문가와 관리들이 저마다 의견을 내놓았어요. 호주 내무장관 토니 버크는 마이크로소프트가 2024년 크라우드스트라이크 장애처럼 업데이트가 잘못된 일을 겪고 있다고 본다고 말했어요. 기술 분석가 루퍼트 굿윈스는 알자지라에 규모는 인상적이지만 전례 없는 일은 아니라고 말했어요. 그는 내부 업데이트 오류가 이런 과부하의 흔한 원인 중 하나라고 말했어요. 보안 전문가 트로이 헌트는 BBC에 이번 장애가 일, 예약, 온라인 계정에 이메일이 여전히 얼마나 중요한지 보여 준다고 말했어요. 더 컨버세이션에 글을 쓴 한 기술 전문가는 사람들과 조직이 자연재해에 대비하듯 디지털 장애에도 대비해야 한다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: For students, the story is a reminder of how much daily life depends on a few shared systems. The Conversation noted that job hunters could not attend planned interviews and that schools could not give online lessons to remote students. It advises people to keep key information, such as contacts, offline and to test their backup plans. Next, watch for Microsoft's full explanation of the cause and for how fast every region returns to normal.
paragraphs.ko: 학생들에게 이 일은 일상이 소수의 공동 시스템에 얼마나 기대고 있는지 일깨워 줘요. 더 컨버세이션은 구직자들이 예정된 면접에 가지 못했고 학교가 원격 학생에게 온라인 수업을 하지 못했다고 짚었어요. 이 글은 연락처 같은 중요한 정보를 오프라인에도 보관하고 백업 계획을 시험해 보라고 권해요. 다음으로는 마이크로소프트가 원인을 어떻게 자세히 설명하는지, 모든 지역이 얼마나 빨리 정상으로 돌아오는지 지켜봐야 해요.

pro.en: A sweeping Microsoft outage that began on Thursday, Nov. 12, crippled email and other workplace tools across the globe, with Outlook bearing the brunt of the disruption. Teams and the Copilot AI assistant were also disrupted, while the outage tracker Downdetector logged complaints from 74 countries and territories within roughly an hour of the first reports. More than 130,000 users reported Outlook problems, although the true figure is probably far higher because such trackers rely on people choosing to report faults themselves. Microsoft says more than 430 million people use its 365 applications, which suggests the potential reach of the failure was enormous.

Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack, attributing the disruption instead to an "elevated load" on part of its infrastructure after a large number of servers abruptly became unavailable. The loss of those servers diverted additional traffic to the remaining machines, straining them further and compounding the original fault. Several restarted servers faltered again once traffic returned, and the company conceded that its first attempts at repair had not taken effect as intended. By Friday morning, Microsoft reported early signs of stabilisation and progress in the Asia Pacific region, while cautioning that intermittent problems could persist for some customers.

The repercussions extended well beyond corporate inboxes, reaching public services in Britain, where GP surgeries, pharmacies, police forces and schools were all affected by the breakdown. Government systems in Singapore and Japan were disrupted, as were the Supreme Court of the Philippines and Australia's spy agency and federal police. In Germany, the rail operator Deutsche Bahn said the breakdown made it difficult to distribute timetables for trains that had been diverted from their usual routes. OpenAI and Anthropic likewise said that connectors linking their AI products to Microsoft 365 were not functioning as expected, showing how outages ripple across companies.

With Microsoft yet to publish a root cause, outside experts and officials offered their own readings of what had gone wrong in the sprawling system. Australia's Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft believed it was confronting something akin to the 2024 CrowdStrike outage, in which a software update had gone awry. Analyst Rupert Goodwins told Al Jazeera that the scale was impressive but not unprecedented, adding that a faulty internal update is one of the common causes of such overload. Security specialist Troy Hunt told the BBC that the episode showed how critical email remains to work, appointments and access to online accounts. A technology expert writing in The Conversation argued that individuals and organisations should prepare for digital outages in much the way they prepare for natural disasters.

For students, the episode illustrates how heavily daily routines rest on a handful of shared digital systems that few people think about until they fail. The Conversation noted that job hunters were unable to attend planned interviews and that schools could not provide online lessons for remote students. Its author urged people to store essential information such as contacts offline and urged organisations to test their backup plans rather than leave them on paper. Attention now turns to whether Microsoft publishes a full explanation of the cause and how quickly service returns to normal across every region.

views.view: Experts warned that the outage could have far-reaching effects because email is still so important for work and daily tasks.
An analyst called the outage very embarrassing for Microsoft, and another said it is mainly a communication risk.
A tech expert says the evidence does not point to a cyberattack and urges people to prepare for outages like natural disasters.
The report follows Microsoft's step-by-step recovery and notes that governments and companies from Asia to the U.S. were affected.
Microsoft said it was not aware of malicious activity, and its first repair attempts were not working as expected.

why: Many people use the same few tools for email and work, so one failure can stop a lot of things at once.

lines.life: If your school, internship or job uses Outlook or Teams, an outage like this can delay messages, so it helps to keep a backup way to reach people.

issues.title: Iran Says It Hit a US Radar in Bahrain After an Attack on Its Port Town
issues.gist: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. It says this answers a strike on a telecom tower in Sirik, and the claim is not yet confirmed.
issues.gistKo: 이란 혁명수비대가 바레인에 있는 미국 조기경보 레이더를 파괴했다고 밝혔어요. 시리크 통신탑 공격에 대한 대응이라고 하지만 아직 확인되지는 않았어요.
issues.easyKo: 이란 군 조직이 바레인의 미국 레이더를 공격했다고 주장했어요. 먼저 자기 나라 항구 도시의 통신탑이 공격받았기 때문이라고 해요. 미국과 바레인은 아직 답하지 않았고, 호르무즈 해협을 둘러싼 긴장이 더 커지고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Friday that it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. Washington and Bahrain had not confirmed any strike, and the claim could not be independently verified. It is the first such claim in months, and the first report of a hit on Bahrain since September.

The Guard called the radar strike a serious warning to the US to stop its strikes. It also threatened a harsher response to any further violations. It also warned companies about oil trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

paragraphs.en: Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. An air war began in February, and Iran has hit US bases in nearby Arab countries, including Bahrain, since then. Iran also tells ships not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its approval, and it often targets oil tankers there. The Guard said a gas tanker hit a mine in the eastern strait after ignoring warnings, but this could not be checked. The United States has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and has helped tankers use the strait.

paragraphs.en: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the United States no longer needs a deal with Iran. He also said that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain asked him to delay wider attacks. Even so, talks mediated by Qatar and Pakistan are still going on. Al Jazeera reported from Tehran that Iran is threatening an unlimited response over the Strait of Hormuz.

pro.en: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps asserted on Friday that it had destroyed a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain, though Washington and Bahrain had not confirmed any strike and the claim could not be independently verified. It was the first such claim to emerge from Tehran in months, and the first involving a facility in Bahrain since September of this year.

The Guards framed the operation as retaliation for Thursday's attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, a port town in southern Iran. They described it as a serious warning to the United States to halt its strikes, and threatened a harsher response to any further violations. The Guards also cautioned companies over oil trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, a fact that lends any strike on its territory considerable weight for Washington and its Gulf partners alike. Since an air war began in February, Iran has targeted American bases in neighboring Arab states, including Bahrain, in retaliation for US strikes. Tehran also continues to warn vessels not to transit the Strait of Hormuz without its approval, and it often targets oil tankers in the waterway. The Guards said a gas tanker had struck a mine in the eastern strait after ignoring warnings, an account that could not be independently verified. The United States, for its part, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and has helped tankers use the strait.

President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Washington no longer needed an agreement with Tehran. He added that Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain had asked him to postpone broader attacks against the country. Mediation by Qatar and Pakistan nonetheless continues. Al Jazeera, reporting from Tehran, said Iran was threatening an unlimited response over the Strait of Hormuz after the US attack.

Because the Strait of Hormuz is a critical waterway for international oil shipments, normally carrying about one-fifth of the world's oil, developments in the Gulf can reverberate well beyond the region. For countries such as South Korea, conflicts at sea may ultimately touch fuel prices and trade, a point that makes distant headlines locally relevant. Observers will now watch whether Washington or Bahrain confirms or responds to the Guards' claim, which has not been independently verified. They will also look for signs of further strikes and for whether the talks mediated by Qatar and Pakistan continue.

pro.en: Spanish artist Rosalía made Latin Grammy history on Thursday, claiming Album of the Year for Lux, her third win in the category and a first for any woman. The ceremony in Las Vegas opened with her own medley of songs, and she left with five trophies in all. The singer was born in Barcelona.

Her single La Perla took both Song of the Year and Best Pop Song, while Lux was named Best Alternative Music Album and the video for Sauvignon Blanc won Best Short Form Music Video. She had previously taken the top album prize for El Mal Querer and Motomami, and in her speech she thanked herself for ignoring those who dismissed her music as too weird.

The night also rewarded other acts. Twenty-year-old Argentine Milo J collected four awards and paid tribute to his country's folk tradition, Karol G won Best Urban Music Album for Tropicoqueta, and Puerto Rican reggaeton veteran Daddy Yankee was honored as Person of the Year, with Janet Jackson presenting him a lifetime achievement award before he performed hits such as Gasolina and Con Calma.

Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh joined Daddy Yankee onstage, becoming the first Indian artist to appear at the Latin Grammys. A fan quoted by the BBC described the moment as a cultural revolution and voiced hope for further collaboration between South American and Punjabi musicians, a sign of how widely music in many languages now circulates among global listeners, including students in Korea.

Lux, which Rosalía released last year to enthusiastic reviews, is also tipped as a front-runner when nominations for the main Grammy Awards are unveiled next week, so observers will be watching closely to see whether her Latin Grammy sweep carries over to the wider industry stage.

issues.gist: Manchester United have named Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick. He leaves the United States men's team to try to lift a club that is 18th in the Premier League.
issues.gistKo: 맨체스터 유나이티드가 마이클 캐릭을 해임한 뒤 마우리시오 포체티노를 새 감독으로 발표했어요. 그는 미국 대표팀을 떠나 프리미어리그 18위인 팀을 일으켜 세우려 해요.

views.view: Pochettino may bridge two camps at United, because his style and his love of Sir Alex Ferguson fit both.

paragraphs.en: Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach on Friday, November 13. The 54-year-old Argentine is leaving his job as coach of the United States men's national team. United sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday, only 15 games into the two-year contract he signed in May. Pochettino signed a deal of two and a half years.
paragraphs.ko: 맨체스터 유나이티드가 11월 13일 금요일 마우리시오 포체티노를 새 감독으로 발표했어요. 54세 아르헨티나 출신 감독은 미국 남자 축구 대표팀 감독 자리를 떠나요. 유나이티드는 목요일 마이클 캐릭을 해임했는데, 5월에 맺은 2년 계약의 15경기째였어요. 포체티노는 2년 6개월 계약을 맺었어요.

sents.en: Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach on Friday, November 13.
sents.ko: 맨체스터 유나이티드가 11월 13일 금요일 마우리시오 포체티노를 새 감독으로 발표했어요.

sents.en: The 54-year-old Argentine is leaving his job as coach of the United States men's national team.
sents.ko: 54세 아르헨티나 출신 감독은 미국 남자 축구 대표팀 감독 자리를 떠나요.

sents.en: United sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday, only 15 games into the two-year contract he signed in May.
sents.ko: 유나이티드는 목요일 마이클 캐릭을 해임했는데, 5월에 맺은 2년 계약의 15경기째였어요.

sents.en: Pochettino signed a deal of two and a half years.
sents.ko: 포체티노는 2년 6개월 계약을 맺었어요.

paragraphs.en: United are 18th in the Premier League table, with one win and eight points from ten games. A 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left fans doubting the club's direction. ESPN reported that United were ready to use a release clause worth $10 million to free him from his US contract. Sources also told ESPN that he was the only candidate the club spoke to directly.
paragraphs.ko: 유나이티드는 프리미어리그 순위 18위로, 10경기에서 1승 승점 8점이에요. 본머스에 홈에서 0-3으로 지고 애스턴 빌라와 4-4로 비기자 팬들은 구단의 방향을 의심했어요. ESPN은 유나이티드가 그를 미국 계약에서 풀어 주려고 1,000만 달러 규모의 이적 조항을 쓸 준비가 됐다고 전했어요. ESPN은 그가 구단이 직접 만난 유일한 후보였다고도 전했어요.

sents.en: United are 18th in the Premier League table, with one win and eight points from ten games.
sents.ko: 유나이티드는 프리미어리그 순위 18위로, 10경기에서 1승 승점 8점이에요.

sents.en: A 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left fans doubting the club's direction.

paragraphs.en: Pochettino has coached Southampton and Tottenham, where he reached the 2019 Champions League final, and also worked at Paris St Germain and Chelsea. The BBC argued that he could bring together two camps at United: fans who want to win at any cost and fans who value the club's old style. The BBC also noted that he has long called Sir Alex Ferguson his inspiration. An ESPN review of his time with the US team gave him a grade of C-plus. The writer said the team matched past World Cup results but did not beat them, and that his time had a mercenary feel.
paragraphs.ko: 포체티노는 사우샘프턴과 토트넘(2019년 챔피언스리그 결승 진출)을 이끌었고 파리 생제르맹과 첼시에서도 일했어요. BBC는 그가 유나이티드의 두 진영, 즉 무엇이든 이기길 바라는 쪽과 구단의 옛 스타일을 중시하는 쪽을 이어 줄 수 있다고 봤어요. BBC는 그가 오래전부터 알렉스 퍼거슨 경을 영감의 원천이라 불러 왔다고도 짚었어요. ESPN은 미국 대표팀 시절을 평가하며 C+ 학점을 줬어요. 글쓴이는 팀이 과거 월드컵 성적과 같았을 뿐 넘어서지 못했고, 그의 재임에는 돈을 좇는 듯한 분위기가 있었다고 봤어요.

sents.en: Pochettino has coached Southampton and Tottenham, where he reached the 2019 Champions League final, and also worked at Paris St Germain and Chelsea.

paragraphs.en: In the United States, Pochettino led the team to the last 16 of the World Cup, where Belgium beat them. He will still coach two games against Haiti before he joins United. U.S. Soccer says it now wants a leader with the talent, experience and belief to match its ambition. For fans in Korea who follow the Premier League, the story shows how fast a top coach's job can change.
paragraphs.ko: 미국에서 포체티노는 팀을 월드컵 16강에 올렸고 거기서 벨기에에 졌어요. 그는 유나이티드에 합류하기 전에 아이티와의 두 경기를 먼저 지휘해요. 미국축구협회는 이제 목표에 걸맞은 재능과 경험과 신념을 가진 지도자를 찾겠다고 말했어요. 프리미어리그를 보는 한국 팬에게 이 소식은 명장의 자리가 얼마나 빨리 바뀔 수 있는지 보여 줘요.

sents.en: In the United States, Pochettino led the team to the last 16 of the World Cup, where Belgium beat them.

paragraphs.en: Pochettino is set to take charge for the first time when United visit Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22. He will begin work at the club's Carrington base on Wednesday. Fans will watch whether he can lift United out of the relegation zone.
paragraphs.ko: 포체티노는 11월 22일 유나이티드가 앤필드에서 리버풀을 상대할 때 처음 지휘봉을 잡을 예정이에요. 그는 수요일 구단의 캐링턴 훈련장에서 일을 시작해요. 팬들은 그가 유나이티드를 강등권에서 끌어올릴 수 있을지 지켜볼 거예요.

sents.en: Pochettino is set to take charge for the first time when United visit Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

pro.en: Manchester United confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach on Friday, Nov. 13, ending a brief search that began when the club dismissed Michael Carrick, whose two-year contract, signed in May, lasted only 15 games. The 54-year-old Argentine departs the United States men's national team and has agreed a deal running for two and a half years.

United sit 18th in the Premier League with a single win and eight points from ten matches, and a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth followed by a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa deepened supporters' doubts about the club's direction. ESPN reported that United were prepared to trigger a $10 million release clause to extract him from his US Soccer contract, and that he was the only candidate approached directly.

Pochettino previously managed Southampton and Tottenham, whom he guided to the 2019 Champions League final, before spells at Paris St Germain and Chelsea. The BBC suggested his tactics and long-professed admiration for Sir Alex Ferguson could reconcile United's rival factions, one prizing results at any price, the other the club's traditional identity. An ESPN assessment of his American tenure awarded a C-plus, arguing that the team merely equalled past World Cup showings and that his time carried a mercenary feel.

In the United States, Pochettino carried the team to the World Cup's last 16, where Belgium eliminated it, and he will still oversee two fixtures against Haiti before leaving for Manchester. U.S. Soccer said it now seeks a leader whose talent, experience and belief match its ambitions, a reminder to Premier League followers in Korea of how swiftly managerial fortunes can turn.

Pochettino is expected to take charge for the first time when United travel to Anfield to face Liverpool on Nov. 22, having begun work at the Carrington training base the preceding Wednesday. Supporters will now judge whether he can lift a struggling side clear of the relegation zone.

pro.en: A lightsaber wielded by Darth Vader in the original Star Wars films fetched $4.875 million at auction on Thursday, according to Dallas-based Heritage Auctions, which billed the event as the Ultimate Star Wars auction. The house described the figure as a world record for any screen-used prop from the franchise. Auctioneers had projected a price above $1 million, so the final hammer price far exceeded expectations.

The saber featured in two celebrated duels between Vader and Luke Skywalker: the confrontation in The Empire Strikes Back in 1980, which contains the revelation "I am your father," and the final showdown in Return of the Jedi in 1983. The actor David Prowse and the stunt performer Bob Anderson each brandished it while portraying the villain.

The prop was engineered for performance rather than display. Its hilt originated as a 1950s British camera flash attachment, and the crew reinforced it to accommodate wooden blades during fight sequences. The effects team later traced the rods' movements frame by frame to produce the blazing red blade seen on screen, and Heritage authenticated the piece by matching a bend and a dent on the hilt to production photographs and film frames.

Heritage's Brian Chanes likened the saber to the Holy Grail for a Star Wars collector, noting that it came from the most iconic sequence in the entire franchise. Vader's saber had set a record for a screen-used prop in 2025, and Luke's lightsaber and severed hand surpassed it in July with a $3.75 million sale, before Vader reclaimed the title this week.

The auction offered 27 lightsaber props in total, including examples used by Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker, alongside a blaster carried by Boba Fett and a Yoda puppet hand. The result underscores how much fans and collectors will pay for tangible fragments of film history.

pro.en: Dolly Parton’s final recorded vocals have been released on “Torn,” the closing track of U2’s new album “Carnaval de Luz,” Variety reported, noting that the country star died of cancer on Aug. 25 at the age of 80.

Billboard said Parton laid down her vocals in June, roughly two months before her death, and signed off on the finished mix before she passed away. Pitchfork reported that the song was co-written by U2, Parton and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, with U2’s longtime collaborator Daniel Lanois contributing pedal steel guitar.

The lyrics dwell on a divided household and a family at war, which Variety interprets as an allegory for a country fractured by politics. Bono told Rolling Stone that Parton “sang her heart out,” adding that he could scarcely believe the performance came from an 80-year-old woman and that it is now nearly unbearable for him to hear.

The album is U2’s first collection of new material in nine years, and Island Records has issued several takes of the song, among them the “Kent Wells Version” and the “T Bone Burnett Take.” Pitchfork added that a separate unreleased Parton recording, “My Place in History,” is reportedly sealed in a vault at Dollywood and due to be unsealed on her 100th birthday in 2046.
For admirers in Korea, the release underscores music’s capacity to bridge generations and borders, and Billboard noted that the band is planning a live tour for 2027.

views.view: It reports the release as Parton’s last words and reads the lyrics as a picture of a politically divided country.
It says Parton gave the song her full effort, and that the track ties the album together.
It describes the sound of the song and notes that it may be her last song but not the last one fans will ever hear.

paragraphs.en: Roger Taylor, the drummer of the British band Duran Duran, has said he will leave the group because his tinnitus is getting worse. Tinnitus is a condition in which a person hears ringing or other noise in the ears. Taylor is 66 years old and has played drums for the band since it formed in Birmingham in 1978. This is the second time he has left, because he also quit in 1985 and came back in 2001.

pro.en: Roger Taylor, the 66-year-old drummer of the British pop group Duran Duran, announced that he is stepping down because of tinnitus, a hearing condition that causes ringing or other noises in the ears and that he says has steadily worsened. He has played with the band since its founding in Birmingham in 1978, although he also left in 1985 before returning in 2001.

Taylor said he had reached the point where he must heed his body and his doctors, while his bandmates Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes and John Taylor said the decision followed careful consideration and medical advice. They added that protecting his hearing and long-term health must now take priority. Taylor said he was departing on a real high, after a successful UK and European tour, a second headline show at BST Hyde Park and induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

The group credited his playing with shaping its sound from the outset, noting that he appeared on ten hit albums and on two number one singles, Is There Something I Should Know? and The Reflex. He also performed on A View To A Kill, the band's 1985 James Bond theme. Producer Nile Rodgers, who collaborated with the band again this year, paid tribute by calling Taylor the consummate gentleman of rock and roll.

The remaining members said they would continue exploring new projects, while stressing that Taylor will always remain part of the family. For fans, the episode illustrates how a health problem can end a long career even for a celebrated musician. The coverage does not name a successor on drums, so that question remains open.

pro.en: SpaceX announced on Thursday that it intends to invest $74 billion in new data center campuses in Texas and Arizona, projects that would rank among the largest of their kind in the United States. The commitment underscores how aggressively Elon Musk's rocket and artificial intelligence company is spending in the global contest for computing capacity.

In Texas, the company plans to put $24 billion into a campus on 444 acres of company-owned land near its Starbase launch site, which it says will generate its own electricity rather than draw on the public grid. In Arizona, a $50 billion campus in Cochise County is expected to create 5,500 construction positions and 1,000 permanent jobs, though it still requires county approval.

SpaceX, which listed this year in the largest initial public offering on record, has rapidly built a business leasing computing power to other AI developers such as Anthropic and Google. Anthropic has committed to pay as much as $120.5 billion through 2029, Google pays $920 million a month, and the AI unit generated over half of revenue in October.

The build-out has proved expensive, with capital expenditure climbing to $19.6 billion in the third quarter, nearly triple the previous year's level, and Musk saying the company had secured $40 billion in debt financing for chips. Chief financial officer Bret Johnsen indicated that heavy outlays would persist, likely totalling $35 billion to $40 billion in the three months ending in December.

Regional reports describe the Arizona site as roughly 750 acres capable of drawing up to 6,000 megawatts at full build-out, paired with battery storage, and as the company's first facility in the state. Observers will now watch for the county's decision on Arizona and for any further regulatory approvals the Texas campus may require.

views.view: The plan is one of the largest data center projects in the US, and it is very costly, with spending rising fast.
The Arizona site is about 750 acres and could use 6,000 megawatts of power, and the project cost was not made clear.

pro.en: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez were named the National League and American League Most Valuable Players, respectively, in announcements made on Thursday night. Each player collected all 30 first-place votes cast by the Baseball Writers' Association of America, making both honors unanimous. It marked the first season in which both MVP winners and both Cy Young Award winners were chosen unanimously.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, batted .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, added a Gold Glove for his defensive work and topped both leagues with a 10.6 fWAR. Four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani placed second in the voting, with Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishing third. The award is the Cubs' first in the National League since Kris Bryant won it in 2016.

Alvarez, 29, captured the American League batting title at .316 and came close to a triple crown, finishing with 42 home runs and 106 runs batted in. Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero placed second, and Kansas City's Bobby Witt Jr. was third. Because Alvarez primarily serves as a designated hitter and contributes little in the field, his candidacy rested almost entirely on his bat. ESPN observed that he is only the second primarily designated-hitting player to win an MVP, following Ohtani in 2024.

Both campaigns drew considerable praise from the press, which highlighted how each player shaped his team's season in a different way. Crow-Armstrong opened the season low in the batting order but was shifted to the leadoff spot by mid-May. Manager Craig Counsell said the club needed a spark on offense, and Crow-Armstrong answered by batting .300 in that role. Alvarez, meanwhile, carried an Astros team that finished 81-81 into the postseason with his production at the plate.

Crow-Armstrong said he hopes to deliver more in pivotal moments after going hitless in seven playoff at-bats this year. For students who follow the sport, the honors highlight two distinct paths to value, the complete all-around player and the pure hitter. With awards week concluded, the offseason turns to contracts and free agency, while ESPN notes that labor negotiations between the league and players still loom over baseball.

lines.life: If you use an AI assistant to plan trips, United flights may need to be booked by you directly.
lines.next: Watch whether other airlines follow United, and how United updates its rules as AI assistants change.

talk.q: Would you let an AI assistant book your travel? Why or why not?
talk.qKo: AI 비서에게 여행 예약을 맡기겠어요? 이유는 무엇인가요?
talk.answer: I would use an AI tool to compare options, but I would book myself. United says sharing account details with AI tools can expose private data. I think it is safer to keep control of my own passwords.
talk.answerKo: 저는 AI로 선택지를 비교하겠지만 예약은 직접 하겠어요. 유나이티드는 계정 정보를 AI 도구와 나누면 개인 정보가 드러날 수 있다고 해요. 제 비밀번호는 제가 지키는 게 더 안전하다고 생각해요.

paragraphs.en: United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf. The airline gave cybersecurity risks and the risk of breaking federal rules as reasons. AI agents are tools that act for a user, for example when someone gives an assistant their login details. The New York Times said the airline announced the move on Wednesday.

sents.en: United warned that sharing account details with personal AI assistants can expose sensitive information.

sents.en: It also said the tools might make unintended purchases, change accounts or use MileagePlus miles.
sents.ko: 또 이런 도구가 뜻하지 않은 구매를 하거나 계정을 바꾸거나 마일리지를 쓸 수 있다고 했어요.

sents.en: The airline will limit access directly on its own platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators.
sents.ko: 항공사는 자사 플랫폼에서는 직접, 여행사와 항공권 모음 사이트를 통해서는 간접적으로 접근을 제한할 거예요.

sents.ko: 예약, 발권, 유통 정책도 고칠 계획이에요.

For example, flight check-in requires a person to confirm that bags do not contain banned substances like explosives. sents.en: United also warned that AI agents could break rules of the Federal Aviation Administration or the Department of Transportation.

sents.en: Those agents can do jobs like booking restaurants and shopping.
sents.ko: 이런 에이전트는 식당 예약이나 쇼핑 같은 일을 해요.

paragraphs.en: TechCrunch called United the latest big American company to keep AI agents out of its systems. Airlines and banks are struggling to tell real customers from AI systems acting for them. Sharing passwords with apps and assistants can create security risks if those logins leak or become exposed. Last week Bank of America urged customers not to share their passwords with their AI assistants. The Times said the move echoes worry that AI agents could go out of control.
paragraphs.ko: 다른 대기업과 은행도 비슷한 걱정을 하고 있고, 걱정은 AI의 통제 문제로 이어져요.

sents.en: TechCrunch called United the latest big American company to keep AI agents out of its systems.
sents.ko: 테크크런치는 유나이티드를 AI 에이전트를 자사 시스템에서 막은 최근의 미국 대기업이라고 불렀어요.

sents.en: The Times said the move echoes worry that AI agents could go out of control.

Watch whether other airlines make similar rules.

sents.en: For students who plan trips with AI tools, this means United flights may need to be booked by the traveler directly.

sents.en: Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately reply to the Times.
sents.ko: 메타, 구글, 오픈AI, 앤트로픽은 타임스의 문의에 곧바로 답하지 않았어요.

sents.en: Watch whether other airlines make similar rules.
sents.ko: 다른 항공사가 비슷한 규칙을 만드는지 지켜보세요.

pro.en: United Airlines said it will restrict access by AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on behalf of users, citing cybersecurity risks and the danger of undermining federal regulations, in a move the New York Times said was announced on Wednesday, with AI agents defined as tools acting for a user, for instance when someone hands an assistant their login details.

The carrier warned that sharing account credentials with personal AI assistants can expose sensitive information and trigger unintended purchases, account changes or spending of MileagePlus miles, and said it will curb access directly on its platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators while revising its booking, ticketing and distribution policies.

United also cautioned that automated agents could violate Federal Aviation Administration or Department of Transportation rules, noting that check-in requires a person to acknowledge that bags hold no banned substances such as explosives, as Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic compete to put AI agents that book restaurants and handle shopping in users' hands.

TechCrunch described the airline as the latest American corporate giant to shut out AI agents, noting that airlines and banks are struggling to distinguish genuine customers from AI systems acting for them, and that Bank of America urged customers last week not to hand passwords to AI assistants, since credentials shared with apps can create security risks if they leak or become exposed.

For students who plan trips with AI tools, the policy implies that United bookings may have to be made directly by the traveler, and the airline said it would keep reviewing its response as the assistants evolve, while the four AI companies did not immediately respond to the Times.

issues.gist: Kia plans to spend $2 billion on a second plant in India. The new factory should begin production in early 2030 and raise Kia's capacity there above 600,000 vehicles a year.

pro.en: Kia, the South Korean automaker, announced on Friday, Nov. 13, a $2 billion plan to open a second manufacturing plant in India as it seeks to boost output in an expanding market. Through Kia India, it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Andhra Pradesh government for a site in Anantapur, home to a Kia factory built in 2019.

Production at the new site is slated to begin in early 2030 with an annual capacity of 200,000 vehicles, which would push Kia's combined Indian capacity past 600,000 units a year. Yonhap noted that the carmaker already sells a spread of models in India, among them the Seltos, Sonet, Syros, Carens, Carens Clavis and Carnival.

Yonhap described the project as one piece of Hyundai Motor Group's wider push to deepen its footprint in India, the world's third-largest car market after China and the United States. The conglomerate announced in October that it would invest a total of $15.5 billion in the country between 2026 and 2032.

For Korean students, the announcement illustrates how the country's manufacturers are spreading production to large overseas markets, which is a useful example for discussions of global business strategy. The date worth watching is early 2030, when the second plant is scheduled to begin production in Anantapur and add to Kia's existing capacity there.

pro.en: Cade Cunningham poured in a career-high 52 points on Thursday night as the Detroit Pistons outlasted the Washington Wizards 144-140 in double overtime. He added 11 assists without committing a single turnover, a combination no player had managed in a game since at least 1978, ESPN reported. Detroit also received the first career triple-double from Ausar Thompson, who finished with 17 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds.

The contest was tight throughout, featuring 20 lead changes, and Cunningham had only 22 points after three quarters before adding 18 in the fourth. Trae Young then drained a three-pointer at the buzzer to tie it at 121 and force the game into a first overtime period. Washington opened the extra period with the first seven points, yet Cunningham answered with a jumper, two free throws and a three to level the score at 130. AJ Dybantsa, this year's top draft pick, pulled the Wizards even once more with less than a second remaining, forcing a second extra period.

In the second overtime, Cunningham sank a three-pointer that put Detroit ahead 135-132, and Anthony Davis fouled out after producing 30 points and 15 rebounds for Washington. A fadeaway jumper from Cunningham later built a four-point cushion with 25 seconds left, and the Wizards had no third rally left. He scored 30 points across the fourth quarter and overtime, the most by a Pistons player since the 1997-98 season.

Washington received three 30-point performances, from Young with 37, Alex Sarr with 30 and Davis with 30, yet still absorbed its sixth consecutive defeat. According to ESPN, Cunningham became only the fifth player since 1977-78 to post a 50-point double-double with zero turnovers, joining Michael Jordan, Moses Malone, Carmelo Anthony and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Cunningham himself said afterward that it was the best he had ever done it in his NBA career, a candid assessment of his play.

For Korean basketball followers, the game illustrates how a single star can decide a marathon contest from start to finish. Attention now turns to whether Cunningham can sustain this form and whether the Wizards can finally end their losing streak.

The Pistons stayed calm to win a tough road game, while Washington lost for the sixth time in a row.

pro.en: Workers across Spain staged their first general strike in 14 years on Wednesday, answering a call by the country's two largest unions over soaring housing costs and the rising cost of living. Unions said millions took part, while hundreds of thousands joined evening rallies in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia and other cities, and roadblocks and picket lines caused serious disruption to transport and public services.

Rents lie at the heart of the grievance: according to the property portal Idealista, a 50-square-meter apartment in Madrid averaged 1,170 euros a month in October, nearly half of Spain's average gross monthly salary of about 2,460 euros and well above the 30 percent threshold commonly recommended by housing experts. Anger deepened after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from the flat she had occupied for seven decades, and she died in hospital weeks afterward.

Roughly 120,000 people marched through Madrid and more than 50,000 gathered in Barcelona, where reports described a festive mood and one participant called the atmosphere largely peaceful. Later, however, a group of masked protesters set rubbish bins ablaze, smashed shop windows and hurled fireworks at officers, who responded with tear gas, and the interior ministry reported dozens of arrests. Electricity demand dropped 7.5 percent in the early hours, against a fall of more than 15 percent during the previous general strike.

Union leaders hailed the walkout as a success, with the UGT's Pepe Álvarez citing massive participation and Unai Sordo of CC OO calling turnout very significant. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his ministers openly encouraged workers to join, whereas the conservative People's Party accused the government of exploiting the strike for electoral gain and its leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, dismissed it as nonsense, and a senior business-group official likewise argued that the action was political rather than labor-related.

Spaniards go to the polls in parliamentary elections on 29 November, which Sánchez called early after parliament declined to approve his housing reform plan, with the strike held a little over two weeks before the vote. For Korean students who pay rent while studying or working, the episode illustrates how housing costs can reshape a nation's politics.

views.view: The BBC reports both the strike and the clashes, and notes the strike came a little over two weeks before national elections.
The NYT says rising rents and stagnant wages have become central issues in the coming national election.

paragraphs.en: Pope Leo XIV returned to Peru on Wednesday, November 11, for the last stop of a 12-day trip to South America. He is the first pope born in the United States, but he spent two decades in Peru as a missionary, priest and bishop. He became a Peruvian citizen in 2015, and in Lima he called Peru his homeland. Local authorities said about 3 million people lined the roads to see him.
paragraphs.ko: 교황 레오 14세가 11월 11일 수요일 12일간의 남미 순방 마지막 방문지인 페루로 돌아왔어요. 그는 미국 출신 첫 교황이지만, 선교사와 사제, 주교로 20년을 페루에서 보냈어요. 그는 2015년 페루 시민이 되었고, 리마에서 페루를 조국이라고 불렀어요. 현지 당국은 약 300만 명이 길가에 나와 그를 보았다고 밝혔어요.

paragraphs.en: On Thursday the pope met six victims of abuse by Church members, including people linked to a lay group called Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The Vatican said he spent over an hour with them and met each person individually. In a speech to bishops, he said the Church must make amends and build a culture of prevention and protection. Pope Francis closed that group in 2025 after years of allegations of abuse and corruption.

pro.en: Pope Leo XIV touched down in Peru on Wednesday, Nov. 11, the final leg of a 12-day tour of South America. The first pontiff born in the United States, he spent two decades in Peru as a missionary, priest and bishop, took citizenship in 2015 and described the country in Lima as his homeland, while local authorities estimated that about 3 million people lined the streets to watch him pass.

On Thursday the pontiff met six victims of abuse by members of the Church, among them people tied to the lay society Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, and the Vatican said he spent more than an hour with them, meeting each person individually. Addressing bishops, he insisted the Church must make amends and foster a culture of prevention and protection, after Pope Francis dissolved the society in 2025 following years of allegations of abuse and corruption.

Leo also turned to the position of women and families, denouncing machismo before a crowd of roughly 40,000 and, as France 24 reported, calling violence against women a reality that wounds all of humanity. Al Jazeera noted that he further cautioned that digital technology risks displacing genuine human interaction and pressed the case for gender equality, while the New York Times read the trip as evidence of the emotional bond he retains with the land that formed him.

A victim who spoke to AFP said many survivors still need support, and Renzo Orbegozo, 50, said they want comprehensive reparation. The US-based group Bishop Accountability, for its part, circulated a list of 77 Peruvian clergy publicly accused of abusing minors, and Pew Research Center interviewed more than 6,100 Latin American adults in spring 2026 to chart Catholic belief and practice across the region.

On Friday, Nov. 13, crowds gathered early in the northern city of Chiclayo, where Leo once served as bishop, ahead of an outdoor Mass that is the centerpiece of his 12-day South American tour. The visit comes less than a month after surgeons removed a lobe of his right lung, the New York Times reported.

issues.title: ICE reports record deportations in fiscal year 2026 as politics heat up
issues.gist: US immigration agency ICE says it deported 483,200 people in fiscal year 2026, a record. The numbers are drawing strong political reactions.
issues.gistKo: 미국 이민세관단속국(ICE)이 2026 회계연도에 48만 3,200명을 추방해 역대 최고라고 밝혔어요. 이 수치를 두고 정치권 반응이 뜨거워요.
issues.easyKo: 미국 이민 단속 기관인 ICE가 올해 회계연도에 역대 가장 많은 사람을 추방했다고 발표했어요. 전문가들은 수치가 완전하지 않다고 말하고, 정치권에서는 이 정책을 두고 의견이 갈려요. 앞으로 의회가 어떻게 나올지 지켜볼 만해요.

views.view: Al Jazeera notes Trump's approval on immigration fell to 38% and Democrats plan to investigate ICE tactics.
ABC News (via AP) reports the record figures and notes the release gave no breakdown of criminal histories.

why: The numbers show how strongly the US government is enforcing immigration law.
They also raise a political fight about how far enforcement should go.
lines.agree: Sources agree the 2026 numbers are the highest in ICE's history.
lines.split: Some officials praise tough enforcement, while others say it has gone too far and want ICE investigated.
lines.life: International students and families in the US may feel the effect of stricter immigration rules.
lines.next: Watch whether Congress investigates ICE and whether the government shares more detail about who is removed.

talk.q: Why can numbers like these be hard to judge by themselves?
talk.qKo: 이런 수치는 왜 그것만으로 판단하기 어려울 수 있나요?
talk.answer: ICE reported 483,200 deportations, but Steven Camarota said it is unclear how many were removals from inside the country. I think we need more detail before we judge the policy. Numbers tell us how big something is, but not always what is inside them.

paragraphs.en: The US government says it carried out more immigration deportations in the last fiscal year than in any year in the history of its immigration agency. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE, said it deported 483,200 people in the year that ended Sept. 30. That is up 9% from the old record of 442,640 a year earlier and up 78% from 271,480 in 2024. ICE also reported about 474,850 arrests, roughly double the 239,890 arrests from the year before. Al Jazeera put the arrest total at more than 491,000.
paragraphs.ko: 미국 정부는 지난 회계연도에 이민세관단속국 역사상 어느 해보다 많은 추방을 했다고 밝혔어요. 이민세관단속국(ICE)은 9월 30일에 끝난 회계연도에 48만 3,200명을 추방했다고 했어요. 이는 1년 전 기록인 44만 2,640명보다 9%, 2024년의 27만 1,480명보다 78% 많은 수치예요. ICE는 체포도 약 47만 4,850건이라고 했는데, 전년의 23만 9,890건의 거의 두 배예요. 알자지라는 체포 건수를 49만 1천 건이 넘는다고 전했어요.

paragraphs.en: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said ICE had been unleashed to find and remove people who are in the country illegally. ICE said it made more than 48,000 arrests in September, after a record of 50,925 in August. The press release did not say how many of the people had criminal records, which earlier administrations had reported. ICE had not given such exact counts since President Donald Trump returned to the White House.

pro.en: The Trump administration reported that Immigration and Customs Enforcement removed 483,200 people in the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, the most in the agency's history. The figure is 9% above the prior record of 442,640 set a year earlier and 78% above the 271,480 removals logged in 2024. ICE also reported roughly 474,850 arrests, about double the 239,890 recorded the previous year, although Al Jazeera put the arrest total above 491,000.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said ICE had been unleashed to target and remove people living in the country illegally. The agency said it made more than 48,000 arrests in September, following a record 50,925 in August. The release did not break down how many of those detained had criminal histories, a detail previous administrations had disclosed, and ICE had not published such precise counts since Donald Trump returned to office.

Steven Camarota, a researcher at the Center for Immigration Studies, told Al Jazeera that enforcement has expanded beyond that of any prior president and that the undocumented population appears to have shrunk, partly because of out-migration driven by fear. He cautioned, however, that the data are incomplete because it is unclear how many cases were interior removals as opposed to people turned back at borders or airports. Trump has conceded his approach may be too tough while defending his record on removing those he describes as dangerous.

The issue has become a liability for the president, with Reuters/Ipsos polling cited by Al Jazeera showing his approval on immigration at 38%, down from 50% at the outset of his term. Democrats, who will take control of Congress next year, intend to scrutinize ICE tactics and broaden pathways to legal status, though they are not united in tone: Rep. Henry Cuellar said Democrats will not be extreme and that he has discussed focusing on criminals with Trump officials, while Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan vowed, "We will rip ICE apart."

For international students and immigrant families in the US, the figures illustrate how much stricter enforcement has become. The next developments to watch are whether Congress opens investigations into ICE and whether the administration discloses more detail about whom it is removing.

pro.en: Following a Veterans Day wreath-laying on Nov. 11 at Arlington National Cemetery, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, his wife Jennifer and several aides posed for photographs near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. When someone in the group laughed, the sentinel on duty turned and ordered the visitors to maintain silence and respect, and a video of the exchange circulated widely.

The sentinel was subsequently identified as Spc. Thomas Iglesias, whom Hegseth summoned to the Pentagon on Thursday to present with the Joint Service Commendation Medal. Members of the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, attended the ceremony, and the secretary published photographs of the presentation on X.

Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the soldier had correctly and respectfully reminded everyone present to observe decorum. According to ABC News, the commendation is awarded to service members who distinguish themselves through meritorious achievement while assigned to a joint military staff, activity or agency.

CBS News noted that such admonitions at the tomb are far from unusual, citing a 2022 Army interview in which a regimental member said sentinels respond to crowds two or three times a day. The BBC added that a soldier has kept watch over the memorial around the clock since 1948 and that it marks the grave of an unidentified soldier killed in the First World War.
For students in Korea, the episode invites reflection on the conduct memorial sites demand of visitors, and it illustrates that codes of respect are expected to bind even the most senior officials.

talk.answer: A memorial honors people who died, so quiet and respect help visitors remember them. In this story, a guard reminded even a top official to keep silence. I think the same rule should apply to everyone.

pro.en: Heartland, a new Netflix thriller, stars Jessica Chastain as Misty Jones, a former country music star who has withdrawn to a farm in Georgia, far from the Nashville industry she abandoned long ago. When her brother appeals for help because his daughter, a rising young singer named Charlie, has vanished, Misty returns to Nashville and becomes an amateur sleuth, questioning those around the missing performer.

Shana Feste, who also made the 2010 film Country Strong, wrote and directed the picture. The cast includes Paul Sparks, Garrett Hedlund, Ross Lynch and Jennifer Nettles, with the singer Carter Faith making her screen debut as Charlie. Polygon notes that Chastain performs her own singing, and it counts the musical numbers among the film's livelier moments.

Reviewers broadly admire Chastain's commitment to the role, yet many are unconvinced by the story built around her. The Guardian judges the film more miss than hit and calls its mystery generic, with a twist that is visible from afar. Variety allows that it can be gaudy fun but never an effective thriller, since the villains are identifiable from the outset. Polygon is the harshest of the three, arguing that the film squanders its unusual blend of western, noir and musical.

For students in Korea, such reviews offer useful English practice, because critics deploy vivid vocabulary to describe a film's strengths and weaknesses. Viewers can also weigh several opinions before deciding what to stream. The reaction of general audiences will be worth watching, as critics and viewers do not always agree.

issues.title: Seoul Says Google Met Security Rules for Exporting Korean Map Data
issues.gist: South Korea said Google has met the security conditions for sending detailed map data of Korea abroad. The news could make competition tougher for local map apps like Naver Map and Kakao Map.
issues.gistKo: 한국 정부가 구글이 정밀 지도 데이터를 해외로 반출하기 위한 보안 조건을 지켰다고 밝혔어요. 네이버지도, 카카오맵 같은 국내 지도 앱과의 경쟁이 더 치열해질 수 있어요.
issues.easyKo: 구글이 한국 지도 데이터를 해외로 옮기려면 군사시설과 좌표가 드러나지 않게 해야 한다는 조건이 있었어요. 정부는 구글이 이 조건을 지켰다고 확인했어요.

paragraphs.en: On Friday, the South Korean government said Google has met the security requirements for sending high-precision map data overseas. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport made the announcement after a review led by the government. The review came after the government gave conditional approval in February to export map data at a 1:5,000 scale.
paragraphs.ko: 정부는 구글이 정밀 지도 데이터를 해외로 옮기기 위한 보안 조건을 지켰다고 11월 13일 밝혔어요.

sents.en: On Friday, the South Korean government said Google has met the security requirements for sending high-precision map data overseas.
sents.ko: 금요일 한국 정부는 구글이 정밀 지도 데이터를 해외로 보내기 위한 보안 요건을 충족했다고 밝혔어요.

sents.en: The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport made the announcement after a review led by the government.
sents.ko: 국토교통부는 정부 주도 협의체의 검토를 거쳐 이를 발표했어요.

sents.en: The review came after the government gave conditional approval in February to export map data at a 1:5,000 scale.
sents.ko: 이 검토는 정부가 2월에 축척 1:5,000 지도 데이터 반출을 조건부로 승인한 뒤에 이뤄졌어요.

paragraphs.en: The review found that Google had put in place steps to stop the exposure of geographic coordinates and sensitive military and security sites. These steps cover Google Maps and Google Earth, on both the web and mobile apps. Google built a control system just for South Korea and added a safeguard that blocks app updates if they might show restricted coordinates. In August, it also signed an agreement to get satellite images processed for security by a government institute through a local partner.
paragraphs.ko: 검토 결과 구글은 좌표와 민감한 시설이 드러나지 않게 하는 조치를 마련했어요.

sents.en: The review found that Google had put in place steps to stop the exposure of geographic coordinates and sensitive military and security sites.
sents.ko: 검토 결과 구글은 지리 좌표와 민감한 군사·보안 시설이 노출되지 않도록 하는 조치를 마련했어요.

sents.en: These steps cover Google Maps and Google Earth, on both the web and mobile apps.
sents.ko: 이 조치는 웹과 모바일 앱의 구글 지도와 구글 어스에 모두 적용돼요.

sents.en: Google built a control system just for South Korea and added a safeguard that blocks app updates if they might show restricted coordinates.
sents.ko: 구글은 한국 전용 통제 시스템을 만들었고, 제한된 좌표가 드러날 수 있는 앱 업데이트는 막는 안전장치도 더했어요.

sents.en: In August, it also signed an agreement to get satellite images processed for security by a government institute through a local partner.
sents.ko: 8월에는 현지 협력사를 통해 정부 기관이 보안 처리한 위성 영상을 받는 계약도 맺었어요.

paragraphs.en: Under that agreement, Google must replace its current images as soon as it receives the processed ones, without changing them. Industry sources say Google chose the navigation company TMAP Mobility to process the base map data.
paragraphs.ko: 구글은 보안 처리된 영상을 받으면 그대로 바꿔 넣어야 하고, 업계는 TMAP이 기본 지도 데이터를 처리한다고 봐요.

sents.en: Under that agreement, Google must replace its current images as soon as it receives the processed ones, without changing them.
sents.ko: 그 계약에 따라 구글은 처리된 영상을 받는 대로 수정 없이 기존 영상을 교체해야 해요.

sents.en: Industry sources say Google chose the navigation company TMAP Mobility to process the base map data.
sents.ko: 업계 관계자들은 구글이 기본 지도 데이터 처리에 내비게이션 회사 TMAP모빌리티를 골랐다고 해요.

paragraphs.en: Yonhap says the results are expected to heat up competition in the local map app market. In October, Naver Map had 31.2 million monthly users, the most in Korea. TMAP followed with 15.1 million, then Kakao Map with 13.8 million and Google Maps with 10.5 million.
paragraphs.ko: 국내 지도 시장 경쟁이 뜨거워질 것으로 보여요. 10월 월간 이용자는 네이버지도가 가장 많았어요.

sents.en: Yonhap says the results are expected to heat up competition in the local map app market.
sents.ko: 연합뉴스는 이 결과가 국내 지도 앱 시장의 경쟁을 달굴 것으로 예상된다고 해요.

sents.en: In October, Naver Map had 31.2 million monthly users, the most in Korea.
sents.ko: 10월에 네이버지도의 월간 이용자는 3,120만 명으로 한국에서 가장 많았어요.

sents.en: TMAP followed with 15.1 million, then Kakao Map with 13.8 million and Google Maps with 10.5 million.
sents.ko: 그다음이 1,510만 명의 TMAP, 1,380만 명의 카카오맵, 1,050만 명의 구글 지도예요.

pro.en: The South Korean government announced on Friday that Google had complied with the security requirements attached to its permission to transfer high-precision map data abroad. A government-led consultation body, convened by the Land, Infrastructure and Transport Ministry, reviewed the company's implementation of the conditions imposed with February's conditional approval for 1:5,000-scale digital maps.

The review concluded that Google had introduced measures preventing the exposure of geographic coordinates and sensitive military and security facilities across Google Maps and Google Earth on web and mobile. It had built a dedicated control system for South Korea and safeguards that block risky app updates, and in August it signed a deal for security-processed satellite imagery.

Under that agreement, struck through a local partner, Google is obliged to swap its existing imagery for the processed images as soon as they arrive, without alteration. Industry sources said the company had selected the navigation firm TMAP Mobility to handle processing of the base map data.

Yonhap said the findings were expected to intensify competition in the domestic map app market, where Naver Map led with 31.2 million monthly active users in October. TMAP had 15.1 million users, Kakao Map 13.8 million and Google Maps 10.5 million, according to the tracker Mobile Index.

views.view: Google met the security conditions, and the result is expected to make the local map app market more competitive.

paragraphs.en: South Korea held a memorial on Friday for Korean victims of forced labor at the Sado mine complex in Japan. It was held at a hotel on Sado Island in Niigata Prefecture, and it was Seoul's own ceremony, separate from Japan's. This is the third year in a row that Seoul has held a separate event. South Korean Ambassador to Japan Lee Hyuk spoke, and nine family members of the victims attended.
paragraphs.ko: 한국은 금요일 일본 사도 광산에서 강제 노역한 한국인 희생자를 기리는 추도식을 열었어요. 행사는 니가타현 사도섬의 한 호텔에서 열렸고, 일본 행사와 따로 한국이 직접 연 것이에요. 한국이 따로 행사를 연 것은 3년 연속이에요. 이혁 주일 한국대사가 추도사를 했고, 희생자 유족 아홉 명이 참석했어요.
